sections.section: A normal link vs a Strait link
sections.markdown:
| Someone taps your link… | A normal link | A Strait link |
|---|---|---|
| App installed | Opens your website, or the app's home screen | Opens the app on the right screen |
| App not installed | Opens the website. The screen is lost after install | Sends them to the store, then opens that screen on first launch |
| On a computer | Opens the website | Opens the website (or a page you choose) |

Opening a screen in an installed app is a **deep link**. Keeping that screen through an install is a **deferred deep link**. [How both work](https://straitlink.in/docs/deferred-deep-linking/).

1. Your workspace gets a link domain, `<your-handle>.strait.link`, and two keys: a publishable key for your app and a secret key for your server ([Keys](https://straitlink.in/docs/keys/)).
2. You create links in the dashboard or with the [REST API](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/).
3. The Strait SDK in your app gets one `onLink` callback for every way a link opens it, and reports each open for Analytics.

Android and web are live. iPhone is in beta. Live service health is on the [status page](https://status.strait.link).

- **[5-minute quickstart](https://straitlink.in/docs/quick-start/)**: see a link open your app on an Android phone.
- **[Pick your platform](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/)**: React Native, Expo, Flutter, Android, iOS, Unity, web.
- **Leaving Firebase Dynamic Links?** [Migrate step by step](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/).

This page uses the shortest path: your app's custom scheme. Verified App Links (no browser in between), deferred links and iPhone come after, in the [go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/).

[Sign up](https://app.straitlink.in/?signup=1) and name your workspace. The name becomes your link domain, `https://<your-handle>.strait.link`. These docs use `acme.strait.link`.

:::warn Pick your handle before you create a link
To change it, go to **Dashboard → Get started** before your first link. After that the handle is fixed, because shared links depend on it.
:::

**You should see:** your link domain and your publishable key (`st_pub_live_…`) in **Dashboard → Get started**.

In **Dashboard → Settings**, fill in two fields:

| Field | Example | Where to find it |
|---|---|---|
| Package name | `com.yourcompany.yourapp` | `applicationId` in `android/app/build.gradle` |
| Custom scheme | `yourapp` | Any short lowercase word your app will answer to |

**You should see:** **Settings saved**. Leave everything else for now.

In **Dashboard → Links → New link**, set the slug to `summer` and the destination to `https://shop.example.com/product/42`. Or from a terminal:

```bash
export SECRET_KEY=st_live_…   # Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys
curl https://strait.link/v1/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "slug": "summer", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/product/42" }'
```

The destination doesn't need to exist yet. Your app only receives its path and query.

**You should see:** `https://acme.strait.link/summer` in your link list (the API answers `201` with that `shortUrl`).

sections.section: 4. Let your app answer to its scheme
sections.markdown:
Add this intent filter to your main activity, using the scheme from step 2:

```xml title="android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
<activity android:name=".MainActivity" android:launchMode="singleTask" android:exported="true">
  
  <intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="yourapp" />
  </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

**You should see:** the app builds and runs as before (`npx react-native run-android`).

sections.section: 5. Install the SDK and log each link

sections.markdown:
Send `https://acme.strait.link/summer` to yourself in Google Messages or Gmail, and tap it on the phone. Don't paste it into the browser's address bar: phones only open apps from links that are tapped.

**You should see:** the browser flashes for a moment, your app opens, and Metro logs a line starting `Strait link: true /product/42`. In **Dashboard → Analytics**, the tap and the app open appear within a minute.

Tapping in WhatsApp or Instagram can show an **Open in app** page first. That's expected: in-app browsers can't open apps directly.

- **Chrome opens the Play Store or the destination instead of the app.** The scheme in Settings and in the manifest differ, or the app on the phone is an old build without the intent filter.
- **The app opens but nothing is logged.** `links.ts` isn't imported at startup, or the app wasn't rebuilt after installing the SDK.
- **`matched` is `false` with `reason: "not_found"`.** The publishable key is from another workspace. More in [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/).

- [Open the right screen](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/receive-links/): route `e.path` with React Navigation, or see [Expo Router](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/expo/). Not on React Native? [Flutter](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/flutter/) · [Android](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/android/).
- [Go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/): verified App Links, deferred links after install, and iPhone.

Android opens your app straight from a link only if your link domain lists the certificate the installed build was signed with. Add all three in **Dashboard → Settings**:

| Build | Certificate | Where to find it |
|---|---|---|
| Local debug builds | Debug key | The commands below |
| Release builds you install yourself | Upload key | Your keystore, or `eas credentials` |
| Anything installed from Google Play | **Play App Signing** key (Google's, not yours) | Play Console → Test and release → App integrity |

```bash
# Native Android project (Android Studio's shared debug key)
keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android | grep SHA256

# React Native, or Expo after `npx expo prebuild`: the project's own debug key
keytool -list -v -keystore android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android | grep SHA256

# EAS Build: choose Android and your build profile; the keystore's SHA-256 is listed
eas credentials
```

Paste them in any form: upper or lower case, with or without colons. We store them as uppercase pairs joined by colons and refuse anything that isn't a SHA-256 fingerprint.

**You should see:** your package name and every fingerprint in the file we host:

```bash
curl https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json
```

Add a second intent filter next to the custom scheme one from the quickstart:

```xml title="AndroidManifest.xml"
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
  <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
  <data android:scheme="https" android:host="acme.strait.link" />
</intent-filter>
```

Reinstall the app (Android checks at install time), then ask the phone:

```bash
adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourcompany.yourapp
```

**You should see:** `acme.strait.link: verified`. Tapping a link now opens the app with no browser flash. If not, paste your domain into the [App Links checker](https://straitlink.in/tools/app-links-checker/).

sections.section: 3. Test a deferred link from Google Play
sections.markdown:
A link tapped before the app is installed reaches the app through the Google Play Install Referrer, so it only works for builds installed from Google Play:

1. Upload a build to **internal testing** in Play Console and add yourself as a tester.
2. In **Dashboard → Settings → When someone without the app taps a link**, choose **Always Google Play** while the app isn't public. (The default sends people to your website when the Play listing isn't live, to avoid Play's "Item not found" page.)
3. Uninstall the app, tap your link, install from Play, open the app.

The first upload and review can take 1 to 2 hours.

**You should see:** the first open lands on `/product/42`, and **Analytics** shows the tap, the install with match method `install_referrer`, and the open.

1. In **Dashboard → Settings**, add your Apple Team ID, bundle ID and App Store ID.
2. In Xcode, add the **Associated Domains** capability with `applinks:acme.strait.link`, and your custom scheme under URL Types.
3. Read [How iPhone install matching works](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/) before you fill in the App Store privacy label.

```bash
curl https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
```

**You should see:** `<Team ID>.<bundle ID>` in that file. iOS fetches it through Apple's CDN, which can lag behind changes. iPhone support hasn't been proven on a real iPhone yet.

sections.section: 5. Put keys and links in the right place
sections.markdown:
- **Secret key**: on your server only, in an environment variable. Create links from your backend with the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/) or the [REST API](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/), never from the app. See [Keys](https://straitlink.in/docs/keys/).
- **Link pages**: add your app name, icon and colour in **Settings → How your link pages look**, so the pages people see lead with your brand ([App Links](https://straitlink.in/docs/app-links/#how-your-link-pages-look)).
- **No website?** A link's destination can be any `https://` URL on a domain you control, such as `https://yourapp.com/product/42`. Only the path and query reach your app. Desktop visitors go to the full URL, and so do people without the app if you chose "always your website", so make sure that page exists.
- **SMS in India**: whitelist your link domain, `<handle>.strait.link`, in your DLT template like any other URL.

**You should see:** no secret key anywhere in your app's source or build output (`grep -r st_live_ .` from the app folder finds nothing).

- **Works on a debug build, opens the browser from Play.** The Play App Signing fingerprint is missing (step 1).
- **The deferred link opens the home screen.** The build was sideloaded, or the app was opened before you tapped the link. The check runs once per install: uninstall and try again.
- **`assetlinks.json` returns 404.** The package name or fingerprints in Settings are empty. More in [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/).

- [Track events and revenue](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/events/): put purchases on the tap that brought them.
- [Analytics: how we count](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/): what taps, opens and installs mean in your dashboard.

Firebase Dynamic Links has been shut down, and `page.link` links no longer open anything. This guide moves the three things that depended on it: **link creation** on your backend, **link handling** in your app, and **the links themselves**.

The guide has three parts. This page plans the move and maps every Dynamic Links concept to its Strait equivalent. [Swap the SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/sdk/) changes your app. [Import and cut over](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/cutover/) recreates your links, switches your backend and checks everything on a real phone.

Search your codebases for the places Dynamic Links touched. Most apps have three or four:

```bash
# Backend: link creation through the REST API
grep -rn "firebasedynamiclinks.googleapis.com" .

# Android and Flutter apps
grep -rn "dynamiclinks\|firebase_dynamic_links\|getDynamicLink" --include=*.kt --include=*.java --include=*.dart --include=*.gradle* .

# React Native, iOS and Unity apps
grep -rn "dynamic-links\|DynamicLinks\|handleUniversalLink" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.js --include=*.swift --include=*.cs .
```

Also list where people still see old links: email templates, push campaigns, your website, QR codes, and SMS templates registered under DLT.

**You should see:** a short list of files and places. Each one maps to a step in this guide.

A Dynamic Link was created by `POST https://firebasedynamiclinks.googleapis.com/v1/shortLinks?key=…` with a `dynamicLinkInfo` object. A Strait link is created by `POST /v1/links` with your secret key, and most fields move across directly:

| Dynamic Links field | Strait API field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dynamicLinkInfo.link` (the deep link) | `longUrl` | Your app receives its path and query |
| `suffix.option` (`SHORT`, `UNGUESSABLE`) | `slug` | You choose the slug; unique per workspace |
| `androidInfo.androidFallbackLink` (`afl`) | `androidFallbackUrl` | Where Android goes when the app can't open |
| `iosInfo.iosFallbackLink` (`ifl`) | `iosFallbackUrl` | Where iPhone goes when the app can't open |
| `desktopInfo.desktopFallbackLink` (`ofl`) | `desktopUrl` | Where computers go |
| `socialMetaTagInfo.socialTitle` (`st`) | `title` | Preview in WhatsApp and other chat apps |
| `socialMetaTagInfo.socialDescription` (`sd`) | `description` | Preview text |
| `socialMetaTagInfo.socialImageLink` (`si`) | `imageUrl` | Preview image (https) |
| `analyticsInfo.googlePlayAnalytics.utmCampaign` | `campaign` | Or keep `utm_*` in `longUrl`; the campaign is read from it |
| Response `shortLink` | Response `shortUrl` | Always share `shortUrl` |

Settings that belonged to the app rather than each link (`androidPackageName`, `iosBundleId`, `iosAppStoreId`) move to **Dashboard → Settings**, once for the workspace.

**You should see:** every field your backend sends has a row above, or appears in the table below.

| In Dynamic Links | In Strait |
|---|---|
| Links on `yourapp.page.link`, owned by Google | Links on your own subdomain, `<handle>.strait.link`. Custom domains are coming soon |
| Apps could create links with the Firebase SDK and an API key | Links are created with a **secret key**, on your server. The app asks your server ([why](https://straitlink.in/docs/keys/)) |
| `androidMinPackageVersionCode`, `iosMinimumVersion` (`amv`, `imv`) | No equivalent. Handle old app versions in your routing code |
| `navigationInfo.enableForcedRedirect` (`efr`) and the preview page | Not needed. We pick the page per device (iPhone "Get the app", in-app browser "Open in app") |
| `iosIpadBundleId`, `iosIpadFallbackLink` | iPads use the iPhone settings |
| Link stats through the Firebase Analytics REST API | **Dashboard → Analytics**, and every tap as CSV from [`GET /v1/export`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/export/) |
| Firebase Analytics `dynamic_link_first_open` | Opens and installs are reported by the SDK automatically; add purchases with `trackEvent` |

**You should see:** nothing in this table blocks your move. If something does, email [support@straitlink.in](mailto:support@straitlink.in) before you start.

Do the steps in this order, so nothing points at a link that doesn't exist yet:

1. **Workspace and app settings**: package name, scheme, SHA-256 fingerprints, Team ID ([go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/)).
2. **Recreate your links**, keeping the old short codes as slugs where you can ([Import and cut over](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/cutover/)).
3. **Ship the app update** with the Strait SDK and your new link domain ([Swap the SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/sdk/)).
4. **Switch your backend** to `POST /v1/links`, then replace old links in templates and on your website.

Because `page.link` no longer works, there's no traffic to move gradually: as soon as the app update is live, new links work end to end.

**You should see:** a written order of work, with the app release date as the one date that matters.

- **Planning around old `page.link` URLs.** They belong to Google and can't be redirected by anyone else. Replace them wherever you still control the text.
- **Putting the secret key in the app** to keep client-side link creation. Create links on your server instead.
- **Releasing the app before the links exist.** Recreate links first, so the first taps on the new build work.

- [Swap the SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/sdk/): replace each Dynamic Links call in your app.
- [Import and cut over](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/cutover/): recreate your links and switch your backend.

sections.page: Migrate from Firebase: swap the SDK
sections.markdown:
Dynamic Links gave you two calls: one for the link that launched the app (and the pending link after an install), and a listener for links while it runs. Strait merges them: you `start()` the client once and get every link in `onLink`, with `kind` set to `direct` or `deferred`.

| Dynamic Links call | Strait SDK |
|---|---|
| Android `Firebase.dynamicLinks.getDynamicLink(intent)` | `links.start(intent?.dataString)` in `onCreate`, `links.handleUrl(...)` in `onNewIntent`, then `links.onLink { e -> }` |
| React Native `dynamicLinks().getInitialLink()` + `dynamicLinks().onLink(fn)` | `links.start()` + `links.onLink(fn)` |
| Flutter `FirebaseDynamicLinks.instance.getInitialLink()` + `.onLink.listen` | `links.start(initialUrl:, urls:, lifecycle:)` + `links.onLink.listen` |
| iOS `DynamicLinks.dynamicLinks().handleUniversalLink(url)` | `links.handle(userActivity:)` and `links.handle(url:)` |
| `pendingDynamicLinkData.link` (a full URL) | `e.path` and `e.params` (already split), or `e.url` |
| `FirebaseDynamicLinks.getInstance().createDynamicLink()` in the app | A call to your own server, which uses `POST /v1/links` ([example](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/create-links/)) |

sections.page: Migrate from Firebase: import links and cut over
sections.markdown:
Gather them in any of these forms, one per line:

- Firebase short links with the long form attached, like `https://yourapp.page.link/abc?link=https%3A%2F%2Fshop.example.com%2Fp%2F42`
- Plain destination URLs
- A CSV with a header row. We recognise `link`, `url`, `destination` or `longUrl` for the destination, and `slug`, `short`, `path` or `key` for the slug.

```txt title="links.csv"
short,link
https://yourapp.page.link/summer,https://shop.example.com/product/42
https://yourapp.page.link/invite,https://shop.example.com/invite?ref=abc
```

No export? Your backend's database or logs usually hold the `link` values it sent to the shortLinks API.

**You should see:** one file with every link you still want to work.

sections.page: Migrate from Firebase: import links and cut over
sections.markdown:
In **Dashboard → Import**, paste the list or upload the CSV. We pull the real destination out of each Firebase link's `link=` parameter, keep the old short code as the slug where we can, and show a preview with any rows that can't be imported (and why) before you confirm.

**You should see:** a preview listing each new `https://acme.strait.link/<slug>` link, then the links in **Dashboard → Links**.

sections.section: 3. Or import them with the batch API

sections.page: Migrate from Firebase: import links and cut over
sections.markdown:
Replace the shortLinks call wherever your backend created links:

```diff title="share.js"
- const res = await fetch(`https://firebasedynamiclinks.googleapis.com/v1/shortLinks?key=${FIREBASE_API_KEY}`, {
-   method: 'POST',
-   body: JSON.stringify({ dynamicLinkInfo: { domainUriPrefix: 'https://yourapp.page.link', link: productUrl,
-     androidInfo: { androidPackageName: 'com.yourcompany.yourapp' }, socialMetaTagInfo: { socialTitle: title } },
-     suffix: { option: 'SHORT' } }),
- });
- const { shortLink } = await res.json();
+ const res = await fetch('https://strait.link/v1/links', {
+   method: 'POST',
+   headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SECRET_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
+   body: JSON.stringify({ slug: `p-${crypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`, longUrl: productUrl, title }),
+ });
+ const { shortUrl: shortLink } = await res.json();
```

The same call in Python:

```python title="share.py"
import os, uuid, requests

res = requests.post(
    "https://strait.link/v1/links",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SECRET_KEY']}"},
    json={"slug": f"p-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}", "longUrl": product_url, "title": title},
)
short_link = res.json()["shortUrl"]
```

Or use the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/): `await links.createLink({ slug, longUrl, title })`. The package name and bundle ID are no longer sent per link: they're in **Dashboard → Settings**.

**You should see:** your backend returns `https://acme.strait.link/…` links, and they appear in **Dashboard → Links**.

sections.section: 5. Check the whole path on a real phone
sections.markdown:
Before you replace links people can see, check one of each kind:

```bash
# What a tap does on each device, without recording a tap
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https%3A%2F%2Facme.strait.link%2Fsummer&ua=android" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https%3A%2F%2Facme.strait.link%2Fsummer&ua=iphone" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

Then, on a phone with the app update: tap an imported link from Messages or Gmail (the app opens on the right screen), uninstall, tap it again, install from Google Play internal testing and open (the same screen on first open). Paste your domain into the [App Links checker](https://straitlink.in/tools/app-links-checker/) too.

**You should see:** the expected `decision` for each device, the app opening on the right screen, and the tap, open and install in **Analytics**.

sections.markdown:
Work through the list from [the plan](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/#1-list-what-used-dynamic-links): email and push templates, your website, app screens, and SMS templates. For SMS sent in India, whitelist `<handle>.strait.link` in your DLT template. Printed QR codes that point at `page.link` can't be changed; reprint them when you can.

**You should see:** a search of your templates and website for `page.link` finds nothing.

sections.page: Migrate from Firebase: import links and cut over
sections.markdown:
- **Imported links open the website, not the app.** The app update with your new link domain isn't installed yet, or your SHA-256 fingerprints are missing ([go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/)).
- **`402` while importing.** The import is past your plan's monthly link limit. Links created so far keep working; upgrade or import the rest next month.
- **`409` for some slugs.** Those slugs already exist in your workspace (often from an earlier run). That's safe to ignore.

sections.markdown:
- [Analytics: how we count](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/): how taps, opens and installs compare with the Firebase numbers you had.
- [Webhooks](https://straitlink.in/docs/webhooks/): get installs and opens on your server, which Dynamic Links never offered.

| Branch | Strait |
|---|---|
| `yourapp.app.link` domain (or your Branch custom domain) | Your workspace link domain, `<handle>.strait.link`. Custom domains are coming soon |
| Link alias / short path | The link's slug |
| `$deeplink_path` (what the app routes on) | The path and query of the link's destination (`longUrl`). The SDK hands your app `e.path` and `e.params` |
| `$canonical_url`, `$fallback_url`, `$desktop_url` | `longUrl` / `desktopUrl` |
| `$ios_url`, `$android_url` | `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl` |
| `$og_title`, `$og_description`, `$og_image_url` | `title`, `description`, `imageUrl` |
| `~campaign` | `campaign` |
| `~channel` | `utm_source` on the destination (that's where Strait reads a link's channel from) |
| `~tags`, `~feature` | `tags` (the feature becomes a `feature:<name>` tag) |
| `Branch.getAutoInstance()` / `initSession` callback | The SDK's `onLink` callback (direct and deferred) |
| `BranchEvent` / custom events | `trackEvent` |

Download your links from your Branch dashboard's link export, as CSV or JSON. The first row of a CSV must be the header row with Branch's field names (`url`, `alias`, `$canonical_url`, `$deeplink_path`, `~campaign` and so on). JSON can be a list of links, `{ "links": [ … ] }`, or one link per line, and link data can sit at the top level or under `data` the way Branch's API returns it.

```txt title="branch-links.csv (shortened)"
url,$canonical_url,$deeplink_path,$ios_url,$android_url,$og_title,~campaign,~channel,~tags
https://acme.app.link/summer-sale,https://shop.example.com/sale/summer,,,,Summer Sale,summer_2026,instagram,"sale,summer"
https://acme.app.link/p42,https://shop.example.com/products/42,product/42,https://shop.example.com/ios/42,https://shop.example.com/android/42,,,,
```

**Slug.** The link's `alias` if it has one, else the last part of the Branch short link (`https://acme.app.link/summer-sale` becomes `summer-sale`), else the Branch link id (`~id`). Slugs can contain letters, numbers, `-` and `_` (up to 64), so other characters become `-`: `Invite%20Friend` becomes `Invite-Friend`. If that makes two different Branch links land on the same slug, the second gets `-2`. A slug that appears twice in the file, or that a live link in your workspace already uses, is shown as a problem and not imported.

**Destination and deep link path.** Strait routes your app by the destination's path and query: a tap on a link whose `longUrl` is `https://shop.example.com/product/42?ref=x` gives your app `e.path = "/product/42"` and `e.params = { ref: "x" }`. So:

- **No `$deeplink_path`:** `longUrl` is `$canonical_url`, else `$fallback_url`, else `$desktop_url`.
- **With a `$deeplink_path`:** `longUrl` is the web URL's origin plus the deep link path. With `$canonical_url = https://shop.example.com/products/42` and `$deeplink_path = product/42`, `longUrl` is `https://shop.example.com/product/42`, and the app gets `/product/42`. A custom-scheme path loses its scheme: `myapp://invite?code=XYZ` becomes `/invite?code=XYZ`. If a link has a deep link path but no web URL at all, enter your website in the import screen and it is used as the origin.
- **Different `$ios_deeplink_path` and `$android_deeplink_path`:** Strait has one in-app path for both platforms, so the Android path is used and the row shows a warning. Make sure both apps handle it.

Because the deep link path may not be a real page on your website, the original web page is kept for people without the app: `desktopUrl` becomes the canonical/fallback URL (unless `$desktop_url` is set), and so do `iosFallbackUrl` and `androidFallbackUrl` (unless `$ios_url` / `$android_url` are set).

**Platform fallbacks.** `$ios_url` → `iosFallbackUrl` and `$android_url` → `androidFallbackUrl`: where someone without the app goes on that platform when your workspace sends them to a website rather than the store.

**Social previews.** `$og_title` → `title` (or `$marketing_title` when there's no `$og_title`), `$og_description` → `description`, `$og_image_url` → `imageUrl`.

**Campaigns.** `~campaign` → `campaign`. `~channel` is added to the destination as `utm_source` (unless it already has one), which is how Strait labels a link's channel in [Analytics](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/). `~tags` become tags, and `~feature` adds a `feature:<name>` tag.

**Everything must be https.** A destination that isn't `https://` stops the row; an optional URL that isn't (for example an `http://` preview image) is left out and the row shows a warning.

**Other fields are not imported.** The preview lists every field in your file that Strait doesn't use, such as `~stage`, `~creation_source`, `$one_time_use` and your own custom link data keys. If your app reads custom link data, put what it needs into the deep link path or its query string before you import.

1. **Import and test.** Import your links, then tap a few on a real phone with the app installed and without it, and on a desktop browser.
2. **Ship the app update** with the Strait SDK and the new verification domain. You can keep the Branch SDK in the same release so old Branch links still open the app for people on it.
3. **Create new links on Strait.** Point your backend, marketing tools and share buttons at `POST /v1/links` (or the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/)). New links live on `<handle>.strait.link`.
4. **Keep Branch active while old links circulate.** Links on `app.link` are served by Branch, and only while your Branch account is active. Replace them wherever you still control the text (website, emails, app screens, QR codes you can reprint), then let the rest age out before you close the Branch account.
5. **Remove the Branch SDK** in a later app release, once taps on old links have dropped off.

If you used a custom domain with Branch, it can't move to Strait yet: custom domains are coming soon. Until then, new links use `<handle>.strait.link`.

- **Analytics history.** Branch's clicks, installs, opens and attribution data stay in Branch. Export the reports you need before you close the account. Strait counts from the day your links and app switch over.
- **The `app.link` domain.** It belongs to Branch. Links on it keep working only while your Branch account is active, and nobody else can redirect them.
- **A Branch custom domain.** Not yet: custom domains are coming soon.
- **Custom link data** beyond the deep link path and query, and Branch settings such as `$one_time_use`, `$match_duration` or journeys and banners. The import lists every field it leaves out.
- **Separate iOS and Android deep link paths.** One path is kept for both.

sections.section: 3. Let the phone hand links to your app
sections.markdown:
**Android**: one intent filter for verified links on your domain, one for your custom scheme (used when a browser hands a link to your app):

```xml title="android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
<activity android:name=".MainActivity" android:launchMode="singleTask" android:exported="true">
  
  <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="https" android:host="acme.strait.link" />
  </intent-filter>
  
  <intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="yourapp" />
  </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

**iPhone (beta)**: in Xcode, add **Associated Domains** with `applinks:acme.strait.link`, and your scheme under **Info → URL Types**.

The verified-link half also needs your SHA-256 fingerprints and Team ID in Settings; that's step 1 of the [go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/).

**You should see:** after a rebuild, this command opens your app:

```bash
adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "yourapp://shop.example.com/product/42"
```

sections.section: 4. Check that the SDK sees the link
sections.markdown:
Add a temporary log next to `start()`:

```ts title="links.ts"
links.onLink((e) => console.log('Strait link:', e.kind, e.route, e.matched, e.path));
```

Run the `adb` command from step 3 again.

**You should see:** Metro logs `Strait link: direct custom_scheme true /product/42`. Then tap a real link from Messages or Gmail: `route` becomes `custom_scheme` (browser hand-off) or `app_link` (verified link).

- **`Native module ... is null` or `PlayInstallReferrer` is undefined.** The app wasn't rebuilt after `npm install`. Native modules need a new build, not just a Metro reload.
- **The `adb` command opens a chooser or another app.** Another installed app also claims the scheme. Pick a more specific one, like `acmeshop`.
- **The callback never fires.** `links.ts` is not imported at startup, so `start()` never runs.

- [Receive links](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/receive-links/): send `e.path` to the right screen with React Navigation.
- [Test](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/test/): deep links, deferred links and analytics on a real phone.

`e.path` is the destination's path (`/product/42`) and `e.params` its query parameters. One `onLink` callback covers every case. Expo Router has its own recipe on the [Expo page](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/expo/#3-route-links-with-expo-router).

sections.section: 2. Subscribe when the navigator is ready

sections.markdown:
When `matched` is `false`, `reason` says why: `not_found`, `expired`, `password_protected`, `no_match` (a first open with no recent tap) or `network`. The app has already opened, so show your home screen. A first open with no link at all is normal: most installs don't come from a link.

**You should see:** tapping a link to a slug that doesn't exist opens the app on the home screen, and `e.reason` is `not_found`.

- **The screen opens twice.** Your link domain is also in React Navigation's `linking.prefixes`. Remove it.
- **Nothing happens on a cold start.** `navigationRef.navigate` ran before the navigator was ready. Subscribe in `onReady`, as above.
- **The path has your domain in it.** Use `e.path`, not `e.url`. `e.url` is the full destination.

- [Events & revenue](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/events/): record purchases on the tap that brought them.

sections.page: Events and revenue in React Native
sections.markdown:
Every time a link opens the app, the SDK reports it once. You don't write any analytics code for this.

| How the app opened | Joined to |
|---|---|
| Verified link tapped in WhatsApp, Gmail, Messages… | The link (also counted as a tap) |
| Browser handed off to the app (`yourapp://…`) | The exact tap |
| First open after a Play install | The exact tap that sent the user to the store |
| First open after an App Store install | The matched tap |
| Your own https links | Host and path only, never the query |

Reports that can't be sent (offline, server busy) are saved and retried on the next start and whenever the app comes back to the foreground, for up to 7 days (100 at most). Each open has an id, so nothing is counted twice. Navigation never waits for a report.

**You should see:** after tapping a link, **Dashboard → Analytics** shows the tap and the app open within a minute.

sections.page: Events and revenue in React Native
sections.markdown:
```ts
import { links } from './links';

links.trackEvent('purchase', { value: 49.99, currency: 'USD' }); // the tap is attached automatically
```

`trackEvent` returns a promise that resolves to `true` when the event was accepted. Use any event name (`signup`, `add_to_cart`); `value` and `currency` are optional.

**You should see:** the purchase at the bottom of the funnel in **Analytics**, with its revenue, on the channel of the link you tapped.

sections.page: Events and revenue in React Native
sections.section: 3. Understand which tap gets the credit
sections.markdown:
The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, an open from a verified short link, or an iPhone install match. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

**You should see:** two links tapped one after the other credit a purchase to the second one only.

sections.page: Events and revenue in React Native
sections.markdown:
- **The purchase shows as direct.** The last link open was more than 7 days ago, or the app was opened without a link since. That's by design.
- **`trackEvent` resolves to `false`.** The phone was offline or the key is wrong. Events aren't queued like open reports, so retry from your own code if it matters.
- **Revenue is counted twice.** You also send the same purchase from your server with the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/). Send it from one place.

`adb` hands your app a URL exactly as the phone would, so you can check routing before anything else:

```bash

adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "yourapp://shop.example.com/product/42?color=red"

# Verified link (needs App Links verified: go-live checklist, step 2)
adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "https://acme.strait.link/summer"
```

sections.section: 2. Tap a real link from a chat app
sections.markdown:
Send `https://acme.strait.link/summer` to yourself in Google Messages, Gmail and WhatsApp, and tap it in each. Phones only open apps from links that are tapped, never from the address bar.

**You should see:** the app opens on the link's screen. In WhatsApp or Instagram you may see an **Open in app** page first: in-app browsers can't open apps on their own, so we show one button that can.

sections.section: 3. Ask what a tap would do, without tapping
sections.markdown:
`GET /v1/simulate` runs the same decision a real tap gets, for any device, without recording a tap:

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https%3A%2F%2Facme.strait.link%2Fsummer&ua=whatsapp-android" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

Presets for `ua`: `android`, `iphone`, `ipad`, `desktop`, `instagram-ios`, `instagram-android`, `facebook-android`, `whatsapp-android`, `bot`. **Dashboard → Playground** runs the same check.

**You should see:** a `decision`, the `location` the phone would be sent to, and a plain-English `reason`. See [Dry-run a tap](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/simulate-tap/).

sections.section: 4. Test a deferred link (first open after install)
sections.markdown:
On Android the link travels through the Google Play Install Referrer, so the app must be installed from Google Play. Internal testing is fine; a sideloaded build has no referrer. Set up internal testing once ([go-live checklist, step 3](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/#3-test-a-deferred-link-from-google-play)), then:

1. Uninstall the app.
2. Tap `https://acme.strait.link/summer` on the phone. Google Play opens.
3. Install from Play and open the app.

**You should see:** the app's first screen is the link's screen, and the event logged in step 4 of Install & set up has `kind: 'deferred'` and `route: 'install_referrer'`. The check runs once per install: uninstall again to repeat it.

sections.page: Test deep links in React Native
sections.section: 5. Check reports and re-run the deferred check
sections.markdown:
```ts title="debug.ts"
import { links } from './links';

console.log('waiting to send:', await links.pendingOpenReports()); // opens saved while offline
await links.flushOpenReports();                                     // send them now
const e = await links.checkDeferred();                              // re-run the deferred check
console.log(e.kind, e.matched, e.reason, e.path);
```

`checkDeferred()` never records an install and doesn't touch the once-per-install flag, so it's safe to call while you debug.

**You should see:** `waiting to send: 0` when the phone is online, and the same answer from `checkDeferred()` that the first launch got.

- **Verified link opens the browser.** The installed build's certificate isn't in Settings. [Go-live checklist, step 1](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/#1-add-every-sha-256-fingerprint).
- **Works in Messages, not in Instagram.** Expected: Instagram's browser blocks apps; the **Open in app** page is the way out. More in [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/).

sections.page: Test deep links in React Native
sections.markdown:
- [Go-live checklist](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/): everything to finish before real users tap your links.
- [Reference](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/reference/): every option, method and event field.

| Option | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `publishableKey` | `string` | **Required.** `st_pub_live_…`, from Dashboard → Get started |
| `endpoint` | `string` | **Required.** Your link domain, `https://<handle>.strait.link` |
| `storage` | `{ getItem, setItem }` | Pass `AsyncStorage`. Keeps the once-per-install flag and unsent open reports |
| `installReferrer` | `() => Promise<string \| null>` | `fromPlayInstallReferrer(PlayInstallReferrer)` for exact Android installs |
| `linkHosts` | `string[]` | Extra hosts that serve your links. With one link domain you don't need it |
| `clipboardBoost` | `boolean` | iPhone only, default `false`. See [the clipboard boost](#iphone-clipboard-boost-optional) |
| `clipboard` | `{ hasProbableWebUrl, readText }` | Clipboard access for the boost: `fromExpoClipboard(Clipboard)` |

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `start()` | Reads the launch link, listens for new ones and runs the deferred check once per install. Call once |
| `onLink(cb)` | Every link event, including ones before you subscribed. Returns an unsubscribe function |
| `onLinkStart(cb)` | A link just arrived and is being resolved (for a loading state). Returns an unsubscribe function |
| `trackEvent(name, { value?, currency?, linkId?, clickId? })` | Records an event. Resolves `true` when accepted. See [Events & revenue](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/events/) |
| `checkDeferred()` | Re-runs the deferred check (debugging). Never records an install |
| `claimHandoff(text)` | Claims a clipboard-boost link your app got itself, for example from Apple's Paste button |
| `pendingOpenReports()` | How many open reports are waiting to be sent |
| `flushOpenReports()` | Sends them now (also happens on start and on resume) |
| `stop()` | Stops listening for links and app-state changes |

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `direct` (a link opened the app) or `deferred` (tapped before install) |
| `route` | `app_link` (verified link), `custom_scheme` (browser hand-off), `install_referrer` (Google Play), `fingerprint` (iPhone install match) or `clipboard` (iPhone clipboard boost) |
| `appState` | `closed` (the link launched the app), `background` or `foreground` |
| `matched` | `true` when the link resolved to a destination |
| `reason` | Why `matched` is false: `not_found`, `expired`, `password_protected`, `no_match`, `network` or `invalid_url` |
| `url`, `path`, `params` | The destination: full URL, its path (`/product/42`) and its query parameters |
| `rawUrl` | The URL the phone handed the app |
| `linkId` | The id of the Strait link |
| `id` | This open's id (not the link's). The same id is on the matching `onLinkStart` signal |
| `ms` | How long resolving took, in milliseconds |
| `at` | When the link arrived (epoch milliseconds) |

| Platform | Method | Precision |
|---|---|---|
| Android | Play Install Referrer | Exact |
| iPhone (beta) | Short-lived device match | Probabilistic |
| iPhone, clipboard boost on (beta) | One-time link from the tap page | Exact |

See [Deferred deep linking](https://straitlink.in/docs/deferred-deep-linking/) and [How iPhone install matching works](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/) for exactly what's collected and how long it's kept.
The SDK is the same one bare React Native uses. Two things differ: link settings go in `app.json`, and you need a development build, not Expo Go.

```bash
npm install github:bazingga08/strait-sdk-react-native#v0.8.0
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage react-native-play-install-referrer
```

`npx expo install` picks helper versions that match your Expo SDK.

**You should see:** all three packages in `package.json`.

Expo Go can't load the native module, and links on your domain open your app, not Expo Go. Build your own app:

```bash
npx expo run:android     # or npx expo run:ios; runs prebuild for you
eas build --profile development --platform android   # or build in the cloud with EAS Build
```

**You should see:** `adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "yourapp://shop.example.com/product/42"` opens your `app/product/[id].tsx` screen with `id` `42`.

For verified links, Dashboard → Settings needs the certificate of each build you install:

```bash
# Local builds (npx expo run:android): the project's debug key
keytool -list -v -keystore android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android | grep SHA256

# EAS builds: choose Android and your build profile; the keystore's SHA-256 is listed
eas credentials
```

For builds installed from Google Play, also add the **Play App Signing** key from Play Console → Test and release → App integrity.

**You should see:** `adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourcompany.yourapp` reports `acme.strait.link: verified` after a reinstall.

- **Links open Expo Go or nothing at all.** You're running in Expo Go. Use the development build from step 4.
- **"Unmatched route" after a tap.** `app/+native-intent.tsx` is missing or returns `path` for your link domain.
- **Works locally, not from EAS.** The EAS keystore's SHA-256 isn't in Settings (step 5).

- [Test](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/test/): deep links, deferred links from Google Play, and analytics.
- [Events & revenue](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/events/): put purchases on the tap that brought them.

`strait_sdk` is pure Dart. Your app hands it the launch link, a stream of later links and the app lifecycle; it resolves short links, runs the deferred check once per install and emits one event per link.

It isn't on pub.dev yet, so add it as a git dependency:

```yaml title="pubspec.yaml"
dependencies:
  strait_sdk:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/bazingga08/strait-sdk-flutter
      ref: v0.8.0
```

Then the helper packages:

```bash
flutter pub add app_links shared_preferences play_install_referrer flutter_timezone
```

[`app_links`](https://pub.dev/packages/app_links) delivers links, [`shared_preferences`](https://pub.dev/packages/shared_preferences) stores the once-per-install flag and unsent reports, [`play_install_referrer`](https://pub.dev/packages/play_install_referrer) gives Android installs an exact match, and [`flutter_timezone`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_timezone) provides the IANA time zone the iPhone match needs.

**You should see:** `flutter pub get` finishes without errors.



sections.section: 4. Check that the SDK sees the link
sections.markdown:
Run the `adb` command again with the app open.

**You should see:** `Strait link: direct custom_scheme true /product/42` in the `flutter run` console.

- **`MissingPluginException`.** You added a plugin and hot-restarted. Stop and `flutter run` again.
- **The link opens a Flutter route like `/summer` that doesn't exist.** Flutter's deep linking is still on (step 3).
- **iPhone installs never match.** The time zone isn't an IANA name (step 2).

sections.section: 3. Understand which tap gets the credit
sections.markdown:
The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, an open from a verified short link, or an iPhone install match. import android.app.Activity
```kotlin title="Share.kt"
import android.content.Intent
import java.net.HttpURLConnection
import java.net.URL
import org.json.JSONObject

fun Activity.shareProduct(productId: String) = Thread {
    val conn = URL("https://api.yourapp.com/share").openConnection() as HttpURLConnection   // your server

    conn.doOutput = true

        val send = Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).setType("text/plain").putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, url)
        startActivity(Intent.createChooser(send, "Share"))
    }
}.start()
```
